title: 2015–16 Zika virus epidemic
summary: Zika virus spread rapidly through Latin America and the Caribbean, with a suspected link between infection in pregnancy and newborn microcephaly. On 1 February 2016 the WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern and called for coordinated mosquito control, surveillance, diagnostics and vaccine development.

as_recorded.value: following a similar cluster in French Polynesia in 2014

where.modern_name: Brazil (proxy pin: the epidemic centred on Brazil and spread across Latin America and the Caribbean)
where.historical_name: Brazil, Latin America and the Caribbean

importance.justification: A WHO-declared international health emergency with wide regional spread and links to birth defects.

sources.title: WHO Director-General summarizes the outcome of the Emergency Committee regarding clusters of microcephaly and Guillain-Barré syndrome
The Emergence of Zika Virus as a Global Health Security Threat: A Review and a Consensus Statement of the INDUSEM Joint working Group (JWG) - PMC

reviewer_note: The sources do not give an explicit start or end date for the epidemic; the 2015 start and 2016 end follow the Wikidata lead and the February 2016 declaration. The sources give the PHEIC date as 1 February 2016 (WHO) and 2 February 2016 (review article). The causal link to microcephaly was described as strongly suspected, not proven.
